variants.name: Core
variants.summary: Play services, the Store, and the framework. The smallest thing that signs in and installs apps.

variants.name: Basic
variants.summary: Core plus the phone, messaging and contacts apps.

variants.name: Omni
variants.summary: Basic plus setup, the keyboard, and the everyday Google apps.

variants.name: Stock
variants.summary: What a Pixel ships with, near enough.

variants.name: Full
variants.summary: Stock plus the rest of what NikGApps packages.

variants.name: Everything
variants.summary: Every package in the release. Where two cannot coexist the first is taken, so this is a starting point rather than literally everything.

variants.name: crDroid official
variants.summary: What crDroid ships as its official package. Maintained by the ROM.

variants.name: crDroid official full
variants.summary: crDroid's full official selection, adding the everyday Google apps.

packages.name: Google Play services
packages.summary: Core Google services. Everything else depends on it. On Android 17 the bulk of it ships as an apex, and the priv-app directory holds only the Chimera modules.

packages.name: Google Services Framework
packages.summary: Device registration and push messaging.

packages.name: Google Play Store
packages.summary: App store and Play Protect.

packages.name: Play Protect verifier
packages.summary: Scans apps as they install. This is also the component Google's developer verification runs through. Leave it out to do without it, or take verifier-block to stop anything installing it later.

packages.name: Block the developer verifier
packages.summary: Stops the verifier ever being installed. It claims the package name with an empty apk signed by a key that was generated once and destroyed, and Android will not replace a package with one signed by a different key. Holds no code. Mutually exclusive with the verifier itself.

packages.name: Contacts and Calendar sync adapters
packages.summary: Legacy account sync adapters, off by default. No Pixel image since Android 13 ships them because Play services handles sync itself; offered for ROMs that still expect them.

packages.name: Google Setup Wizard
packages.summary: Replaces the ROM's first-boot flow. Needed to sign in during setup; without it you sign in from Settings afterwards.

packages.name: Setup language picker
packages.summary: Lets the setup wizard's language and region step work on ROMs whose Settings has no Google locale picker: it answers that intent and hands off to the ROM's own picker. Tiny, and harmless without the setup wizard.

packages.name: Google Restore
packages.summary: Restores apps and settings from a previous device during setup.

packages.name: Search engine selector
packages.summary: The search engine choice screen shown during setup in the EEA.

packages.name: Google Phone
packages.summary: Call screening and spam protection.

packages.name: Google Messages
packages.summary: RCS-capable SMS client.

packages.name: Google Contacts
packages.summary: Google Contacts, with account sync and caller ID.

packages.name: Gboard
packages.summary: Keyboard, including the offline speech and CJK models. Those live outside the app directory; without them voice typing only works online and Japanese, Korean and Chinese input is degraded.

packages.name: Google Text-to-Speech
packages.summary: Text to speech, including the offline voice data. That lives outside the app directory; without it only languages downloaded on demand will speak.

packages.name: Google app and Assistant
packages.summary: Search, Assistant and the at-a-glance widget. Large (~350 MB).

packages.name: Gemini
packages.summary: Google's assistant. Replaces the older Assistant surface.

packages.name: Trichrome shared library
packages.summary: Shared code Chrome and the Google WebView both need. Each declares it with uses-static-library and neither loads without it, so it is its own package rather than living inside either.

packages.name: Chrome
packages.summary: Chrome. Needs the Trichrome library, which is pulled in for you.

packages.name: Google WebView
packages.summary: The system WebView every app uses to render web content. Also needs Trichrome.

packages.name: Files by Google
packages.summary: Files by Google, the file manager.

packages.name: Google document picker
packages.summary: Replaces the AOSP file picker. This is what every app opens when it asks you to choose a file.

packages.name: Google storage manager
packages.summary: The storage cleanup flow Settings opens when space runs low.

packages.name: Google Photos
packages.summary: Google Photos, with backup and the built-in editor.

packages.name: Markup
packages.summary: The annotation editor Photos and screenshots open.

packages.name: Gmail
packages.summary: Gmail.

packages.name: Google Maps
packages.summary: Google Maps, including navigation.

packages.name: Location History
packages.summary: Timeline, which records where the phone has been. Off until you turn it on.

packages.name: Google Drive
packages.summary: Google Drive.

packages.name: Google Calendar
packages.summary: Google Calendar.

packages.name: Google Meet
packages.summary: Google Meet.

packages.name: Google Calculator
packages.summary: Google Calculator.

packages.name: Google Clock
packages.summary: Google Clock, with alarms and timers.

packages.name: Pixel Recorder
packages.summary: Pixel Recorder, with on-device transcription.

packages.name: Pixel sounds
packages.summary: Pixel ringtones, alarms and notification sounds. Includes the picker that exposes them.

packages.name: Pixel Launcher
packages.summary: Pixel home screen, which on Android 16 and newer needs support from the ROM to start at all. Pair with gsa for the search bar. Without that support it crash-loops on launch, and because it replaces the ROM's own launcher the phone is left with no home screen.

packages.name: Pixel wallpapers
packages.summary: The Pixel wallpaper collections and the picker for them.

packages.name: Emoji wallpaper
packages.summary: Emoji wallpaper. Builds a pattern from emoji you choose.

packages.name: Pixel themes
packages.summary: Pixel icon packs and theming options for the launcher.

packages.name: Now Playing
packages.summary: Now Playing, which names music around you on the lock screen. Works offline once its database downloads.

packages.name: Device Personalization Services
packages.summary: On-device personalisation. App suggestions, smart text selection, Now Playing and Live Caption all route through it.

packages.name: AICore
packages.summary: On-device foundation models the newer Pixel features build on.

packages.name: Google Wallet quick access
packages.summary: The Wallet tile in quick settings, for cards and passes.

packages.name: Digital car key
packages.summary: Time sync for the digital car key, which lets a phone unlock and start a car. Only on devices with ultra-wideband hardware, so absent from a-series and base models.

packages.name: Digital Wellbeing
packages.summary: Digital Wellbeing, with screen time and bedtime mode.

packages.name: Android Auto
packages.summary: A stub. Play installs the real Android Auto over it on first use, which is how a Pixel does it; the full app is not in the factory image to take.

packages.name: Google Partner Setup
packages.summary: Carrier and retail setup hooks used during first boot.

packages.name: Carrier Setup
packages.summary: Carrier provisioning, including RCS and Wi-Fi calling setup.

packages.name: eSIM support
packages.summary: Needed for eSIM provisioning on most carriers.

packages.name: Android Device Policy
packages.summary: Work profile and managed device support.

packages.name: Google Feedback
packages.summary: Reports problems to Google. Harmless to leave out.

packages.name: Credential Manager
packages.summary: Passkey and password autofill support.

packages.name: TalkBack
packages.summary: Screen reader. The one accessibility service most users need.

packages.name: Switch Access
packages.summary: Control the device with switches rather than the touchscreen.

packages.name: Voice Access
packages.summary: Control the device by voice.

packages.name: Sound Amplifier
packages.summary: Amplifies and filters audio through headphones.
